note: Local coverage only. All 66 accepted cases retained; external gates are separate. See compatibility.md for exact identities.

cases.scenario: Spawn without an earlier catalog call
cases.required: Works with a valid explicit model; no init gate

cases.scenario: No skills requested
cases.required: No skill bodies or unrelated descriptions in worker context

cases.scenario: Two skills suggested, worker reads neither
cases.required: Run can complete; no corrective loop or forced loading

cases.scenario: Global/project workflow resources installed
cases.required: Unselected resources and system overrides do not enter the worker context

cases.scenario: Model unavailable or requested thinking gets clamped
cases.required: Clear failure; no substitute model or silent setting change

cases.scenario: Same accepted spawn request repeated
cases.required: Same session/run; one launch

cases.scenario: Same key with different input
cases.required: Idempotency conflict; no launch

cases.scenario: Two continuations race on one session
cases.required: Only one admitted; other receives current state/stale conflict

cases.scenario: Host observes an active run repeatedly
cases.required: No new turn, skill read, or model call

cases.scenario: Observe wait expires
cases.required: Worker remains active; timeout is explicit

cases.scenario: Worker asks a question
cases.required: Visible pending question; exact reply unblocks the original tool call

cases.scenario: Steer sent while worker is blocked on a question
cases.required: Explicit instruction to use reply; no deadlock hidden as delivery

cases.scenario: Worker proposes a reusable lesson
cases.required: Proposal persisted; skills, prompts, and AGENTS.md unchanged

cases.scenario: Worker tool action completes but agent continues
cases.required: Run remains running; not marked completed early

cases.scenario: Cancel during provider call, shell, or question
cases.required: Prompt/tool waits terminate; managed processes cleaned; status honest

cases.scenario: One worker crashes
cases.required: Siblings/server remain usable; crashed run not falsely completed

cases.scenario: Supervisor dies after acceptance
cases.required: Restart does not replay; original receipt remains queryable

cases.scenario: Safe persisted session continued after restart
cases.required: Same conversation from validated checkpoint, new run ID

cases.scenario: Corrupt/unsafe partial session
cases.required: No fabricated tool result or blind replay; clear recovery limitation

cases.scenario: Unavailable modality or bad image input
cases.required: Explicit rejection; no silent image drop

cases.scenario: Tool not granted / path outside allowed file roots
cases.required: The callable tool surface or guardrail rejects it; skills without a reader do not gain tools implicitly

cases.scenario: Shell explicitly granted
cases.required: Actual OS sandbox is established; source is read-only absent a separate grant; scope/backend/policy are reported accurately

cases.scenario: Duplicate worker event or reply
cases.required: No duplicate question, message, or side effect from re-delivery

cases.scenario: Long output, Unicode, and event pagination
cases.required: Explicit truncation and lossless valid UTF-8 pagination

cases.scenario: Cleanup/GC followed by reuse of an old request key
cases.required: Tombstone prevents accidental new work

cases.scenario: Request or skill metadata contains literal slash commands
cases.required: No automatic template/skill command expansion

cases.scenario: Valid fresh spawn using a different configured provider
cases.required: No task-specific role or routing code is required

cases.scenario: Active-run cap reached
cases.required: Explicit admission failure; no hidden queue or unbounded process creation

cases.scenario: External credential text appears in errors/log inputs
cases.required: Recognized secrets redacted; credentials absent from manifests

cases.scenario: Main agent chooses not to delegate
cases.required: No hook or mandatory workflow forces pi-spoke use
cases.scope: Structural inspection and public MCP tests; actual Linux Codex host exercise remains unrun.

cases.scenario: Default operator config; request `bash`, `edit`, or `write`
cases.required: Explicit tool rejection before inference; no helper launched; no authority inherited from other config fields

cases.scenario: Operator allows editing; spawn omits file-write roots
cases.required: `WRITE_SCOPE_REQUIRED`; adding the tool alone does not authorize the workspace

cases.scenario: Request a root partly or wholly outside the operator ceiling
cases.required: Whole request rejected; no silent intersection, clamping, widening, or fallback

cases.scenario: Enable `bash` with empty shell-write roots
cases.required: Effective shell has read-only project plus private scratch; file-edit grants do not alter it

cases.scenario: Delete source using `rm`, absolute `/bin/rm`, interpreter unlink, and directory removal
cases.required: All source mutations blocked by the OS boundary, with canaries unchanged

cases.scenario: Truncate/overwrite source using shell redirection, Python/Node file APIs, and rename replacement
cases.required: Denied under source-read-only shell; testing only `rm` is insufficient

cases.scenario: Modify an outside-root file, including a second configured workspace
cases.required: Denied through shell and structured tools; access to one workspace does not authorize all workspaces

cases.scenario: Perform an authorized structured edit while shell cannot edit the same path
cases.required: Structured change succeeds; shell attempts fail; diffs and policy hashes identify the two paths of authority

cases.scenario: Authorized structured write creates a file in an existing allowed parent
cases.required: Succeeds without granting shell write rights; target guard and OS helper are actually exercised

cases.scenario: Authorized `write` empties an ordinary allowed file
cases.required: The test may succeed: record that permitted writes can destroy content. Do not mislabel the system “no data loss”

cases.scenario: Write and delete a scratch file
cases.required: Allowed only in the invocation/run-owned scratch; private state and other workers' scratch remain protected

cases.scenario: Write or delete unrelated host `/tmp` / `/private/tmp` canaries
cases.required: Denied; upstream implicit temporary grants cannot expose broad shared host temporary storage

cases.scenario: Explicit existing build-output shell-write root
cases.required: Output creation/removal works there; neighboring source/metadata stays protected. Missing root is rejected, not silently created

cases.scenario: Broad workspace shell-write with protected paths absent
cases.required: Enforcement blocks creation/replacement of the protected paths, or the policy is rejected before launch. No placeholder files appear in the real repo

cases.scenario: Write, delete, or rename existing `.git`, `.codex`, `.agents`, `.pi`, `.pi-spoke`, and project instruction fixtures
cases.required: Denied for guarded mutations and shell grants that advertise protection; test ancestor replacement as well as direct access

cases.scenario: Worktree `.git` file points to metadata/common directory outside `cwd`
cases.required: Visible pointer and resolved targets protected; metadata discovery runs no repository hook or custom command

cases.scenario: Modify selected skill, operator config, installed helper, auth/model file, or saved state
cases.required: Denied. Improvement proposals and suggested skills do not unlock protected resources

cases.scenario: Traversal, sibling-prefix confusion, trailing slash, Unicode names, and macOS canonical aliases
cases.required: Correct roots used; no string-prefix escape; valid in-root paths continue to work

cases.scenario: Existing and newly introduced symlinks point from allowed paths to protected/outside paths
cases.required: No out-of-scope write/read through aliases; structured mutation rejects unsafe symlink components

cases.scenario: Hard-link/mount alias would expose protected/out-of-root inode under a writable path
cases.required: Mutation denied or unsafe topology rejected; mandatory scratch-only source protection must still be demonstrable

cases.scenario: Swap a target/ancestor during a structured operation; overlap pi-spoke edits
cases.required: Identity/conflict detection or OS root restriction prevents an out-of-scope mutation; report limitations for hostile external races, never false atomicity

cases.scenario: Nested and newly named protected metadata/instruction targets below normal scan depth
cases.required: Structured guard rejects at operation time; shell policy either enforces the claimed exclusions or is rejected as unsupported

cases.scenario: Read fake secrets after re-allowing a workspace inside a broader denied home root
cases.required: Nested credential/state deny remains effective; rename-to-read bypass is blocked; selected normal source/skills remain readable

cases.scenario: Tool environment/descriptor inspection
cases.required: No provider key, auth cookie, preload/startup injection variable, SSH-agent socket, or supervisor control descriptor is inherited

cases.scenario: Shell/helper network through direct IPv4/IPv6, proxy variables, loopback, DNS paths, or bind/listen
cases.required: Denied as specified; no successful connection to controlled listeners; trusted Pi fake-provider call still works separately

cases.scenario: Unix sockets, Docker/agent socket fixtures, and macOS Apple Events/Launch Services
cases.required: No access to privileged host services; required missing controls cause failure before execution, not warning-only downgrade
cases.scope: Unix sockets denied on Linux; Apple Events and Launch Services not applicable on Linux.

cases.scenario: Missing/invalid SRT config, missing binary, unavailable namespace, or required seccomp failure
cases.required: `SANDBOX_UNAVAILABLE`, `SANDBOX_SETUP_FAILED`, or `SANDBOX_POLICY_UNSUPPORTED`; never raw execution or implicit backend defaults

cases.scenario: Two simultaneous invocations with different roots; shell and writer run concurrently
cases.required: Separate launcher configuration and policy hash; neither receives the other's writable roots, proxy state, or credentials

cases.scenario: Attempt alternate stock Pi callbacks, search-tool executable substitution, or helper command/module injection
cases.required: All active definitions use guarded paths; trusted absolute binaries; fixed helper payload is treated as data

cases.scenario: Invalid policy, path alias, or operator revocation on continuation
cases.required: `POLICY_CHANGED` or specific permission/sandbox error; no inherited stale authority and no new grant from a reply/steer

cases.scenario: File/shell operation denied, then retried via main reply or auto-retry machinery
cases.required: Existing grant remains unchanged; no automatic retry outside the sandbox or policy escalation

cases.scenario: Cancel/host disconnect during shell, helper startup, subprocess, or double-fork/`setsid` fixture
cases.required: All descendants stay restricted; clean termination is verified or reported unconfirmed. No false `cancelled`/cleanup claim

cases.scenario: Crash after invocation acceptance or file mutation but before acknowledgment
cases.required: Invocation receipt survives; unknown side effect is not replayed; safe continuation requires policy and cleanup revalidation

cases.scenario: Ordinary command failure versus observed sandbox denial
cases.required: Typed error distinction is truthful; no every-error-is-sandbox-denied classifier; diagnostics contain no secrets

cases.scenario: Backend upgrade, changed binary, or altered policy compiler
cases.required: Cached capability proof invalidated; pinned compatibility and real-OS negative tests rerun before enabling execution

cases.scenario: Version-1 permissive config or unsafe fallback/network/weaker flags in version 2
cases.required: Explicit migration/validation error; primary shipped example is enforced read-only and cannot authorize shell by omission

release_gates.skip_reason: macOS Launch Services is not applicable on Linux

release_gates.reason: Direct OpenRouter Nemotron and gateway Gemini passed sandboxed read and native continuation; Gemini image input passed. All cleanup confirmed; temporary credentials removed.
Linux stdio transport exposes all six tools and pi_spoke_linux is registered. Actual Codex calls await tool reload; transport discovery is not host verification.
